## EmbeddedCommandInterpreterSpec interface

A data-only description of one shell interpreter whose `-c` option makes the next operand a command string run by that shell (`bash -c 'rm x'`<!-- -->). Like `env -S`<!-- -->, the command that runs lives \*inside\* an operand, so [resolveArgv0()](./sh-ast-analyze.resolveargv0.md) reports `'embedded-command'` instead of the interpreter's own name as the effective command.

Only the option grammar needed to decide \*whether `-c` is an option\* is described: which options consume an operand word (so that `-o c` or `-o pipefail -c` are not misread) and where option parsing ends. Everything else about the interpreter — what its other options mean, whether a given option name is valid — is irrelevant to that decision and unmodeled; an invalid invocation that a real shell would reject is still reported conservatively, since nothing is guessed about what it would run.

Option parsing ends at the first statically known word that is not an option, at `--`<!-- -->, and at a lone `-`<!-- -->; afterwards a word shaped like `-c` is an ordinary script operand. A dynamic word in option position leaves the question undecidable, so scanning stops and the interpreter is reported exactly as before (its own static name). In that case `static: true` means only that the interpreter's name is known; it does not mean the command is a plain shell invocation, because `bash "$f" -c x` runs `x` when `$f` is `-x`<!-- -->.

This shape may grow new optional fields in a \*\*minor\*\* release; existing fields' meaning never changes.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export interface EmbeddedCommandInterpreterSpec 
```

The interpreter's name, matched against a static command word's final path segment: `bash`<!-- -->, `/bin/bash` and `/usr/local/bin/bash` all match `['bash']`<!-- -->. This deliberately differs from [WrapperSpec.names](./sh-ast-analyze.wrapperspec.names.md)<!-- -->' exact-name policy, because a path-qualified shell is the same interpreter and the question here is only whether a command string is embedded, not which executable would be located.

</td><td>

How an [EmbeddedCommandInterpreterSpec.operandOptions](./sh-ast-analyze.embeddedcommandinterpreterspec.operandoptions.md) letter receives its operand inside a clustered word:

- `'separate-word'` — always the next word; remaining letters in the cluster are still options (`bash -oc errexit 'cmd'` is `-o errexit -c`<!-- -->). - `'rest-of-cluster'` — the remainder of the word if any, else the next word; later letters in the same word are part of the operand (`zsh -oc` names an option `c`<!-- -->).


</td></tr>
